scope: Read-only source and practice coverage review; no fresh platform submission or complete re-verification of every statement.

entries.title: First Unique Character in a String
Group Anagrams
entries.prerequisite: Be comfortable with frequency counts and hashable tuples from Python; the restricted alphabet makes a count-based key possible without a sorting lesson.

entries.title: Product of Array Except Self
entries.prerequisite: Prefix/suffix accumulation and loop-invariant reasoning; these are an extension beyond this storage lesson.

entries.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
entries.prerequisite: Two-pointer/sliding-window invariants. Learn that pattern before using this as a timed exercise.

entries.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
entries.prerequisite: Prefix sums and the difference-of-prefixes identity. Negative values rule out a simple monotone shrinking-window assumption.

entries.title: Min Stack
entries.prerequisite: Stack invariants, duplicate handling and per-operation cost accounting.

entries.title: LRU Cache
entries.prerequisite: Hash maps, doubly linked updates and the lesson’s LRU trace. The OrderedDict version is a useful baseline; hand-built node coordination is the extension.

Insert into a Binary Search Tree
Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
entries.prerequisite: BST search and the meaning of ancestor/descendant. The statement guarantees both target nodes exist and allows a target itself to be the ancestor.

entries.title: Balanced Binary Tree
entries.prerequisite: Subtree height/depth and postorder reasoning. This checks height balance; it does not implement rotations or make a tree balanced.

entries.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
entries.prerequisite: Preorder/inorder, recursive divide-and-conquer and array ranges. Revisit Complexity Analysis & Recursion and Backtracking & Divide-and-Conquer as needed.

Kth Largest Element in an Array
Search Suggestions System
entries.prerequisite: Trie prefix traversal and lexicographic ordering. A sorted/filtering baseline is useful before implementing stored top suggestions or ordered subtree enumeration.

entries.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
entries.prerequisite: Merge Two Sorted Lists, heap push/pop and a tie policy for equal priorities whose node objects are not orderable.

entries.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
entries.prerequisite: Trie terminal markers plus DFS/backtracking. Return after Graphs: Representations, BFS & DFS or Backtracking & Divide-and-Conquer if branching search is unfamiliar.

entries.title: Find Median from Data Stream
entries.prerequisite: Min/max heap interfaces, median for odd/even counts, and reasoning about two simultaneous invariants.

entries.title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
Clone Graph
entries.prerequisite: OOP node construction, dictionary lookup and the distinction between aliasing and copying from earlier lessons.

entries.title: Rotting Oranges
entries.prerequisite: Single-source BFS layers. Extend the initial frontier to every starting source; no weighted-shortest-path algorithm is required.

entries.title: Is Graph Bipartite?
entries.prerequisite: BFS/DFS over disconnected graphs plus the definition of a bipartition: every edge must cross between the two groups.

entries.title: Course Schedule
entries.prerequisite: Directed-cycle detection with active/finished DFS states, or indegrees and topological processing. These extend basic BFS/DFS and need a separate correctness argument.

entries.title: All Paths From Source to Target
entries.prerequisite: DFS/backtracking, path-local state and output-sensitive analysis. Backtracking & Divide-and-Conquer is the natural follow-up if restoring a partial path is new.

Accounts Merge
entries.prerequisite: Dictionaries and sets from earlier programming/DSA topics; Python sorted for the required email order. The lesson’s record-grouping example returns indices, so this problem adds collecting and ordering identifiers.

entries.title: Number of Steps to Reduce a Number to Zero
Pow(x, n)
entries.prerequisite: The exponentiation example, reciprocal arithmetic and floating-point rounding. The problem constrains zero-base cases differently from the lesson’s integer example.

entries.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
entries.prerequisite: Binary-tree children and the earlier Trees lesson. The statement counts nodes along a longest root-to-leaf route.

entries.title: Climbing Stairs
entries.prerequisite: Counting disjoint possibilities and the memoization/iteration bridge in this lesson.

entries.title: Binary Search
entries.prerequisite: The statement uses a nonempty array with unique values; the local boundary function also handles empty and duplicate inputs.

entries.title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
Sort an Array
entries.prerequisite: Read the optional iterative heapsort implementation for the statement’s smallest-space objective. The lesson’s buffer-based mergesort uses linear auxiliary space; built-in sorting is disallowed here.

entries.title: Merge Sorted Array
entries.prerequisite: The first m entries are real input; reserved trailing zeroes are capacity, while zero can also be a legitimate input value.

entries.title: Merge Intervals
entries.prerequisite: The official contract merges touching endpoints. Treat these as closed intervals; do not import a different meeting-room endpoint policy.

entries.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
entries.prerequisite: Return 1-based indices, never reuse one position, and account for the statement’s exactly-one-solution promise.

entries.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
entries.prerequisite: The statement uses positive values and returns zero when no interval qualifies; the local implementation returns an optional half-open interval.

entries.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
entries.prerequisite: Previously an Arrays preview; the uniqueness-window mechanism is taught here. The statement distinguishes substring from subsequence.

entries.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
entries.prerequisite: Previously an Arrays preview; use this lesson’s prefix-frequency derivation rather than applying the positive-window rule.

entries.title: Koko Eating Bananas
entries.prerequisite: The official constraints guarantee at least one hour per pile. Contrast this with the local impossible-budget state.

entries.title: N-Queens
entries.prerequisite: The queen investigation, r−c/r+c diagonal keys, choose/undo restoration and generating the required string rows from column positions.

entries.title: Assign Cookies
entries.prerequisite: Use the local threshold-matching exercise and proof. The statement uses positive sizes and returns only a count; the local program also returns original assignment identities.

entries.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
entries.prerequisite: The official statement permits touching endpoints and requires start < end. Equal intervals are separate occurrences; do not deduplicate them before counting removals.

entries.title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
entries.prerequisite: Read the independent covering-points exercise. Both interval endpoints are included here, so an arrow at a shared endpoint can cover both intervals.

entries.title: Jump Game
entries.prerequisite: The input is nonempty and each number is a maximum permitted forward jump, so shorter jumps are legal. The local empty-input return is an additional API convention.

entries.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
entries.prerequisite: State sufficiency and simultaneous old/new state updates from this lesson; read the public buy/sell/cooldown contract before modeling it.

entries.title: Unique Paths III
entries.prerequisite: Backtracking path-local used sets, grid adjacency and this lesson’s subset+endpoint state. Adapt optimization to counting and enforce the designated end condition.

entries.title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
entries.prerequisite: Official endpoints are both included and the input is nonempty. Translate [left,right] to the lesson’s [left,right+1).

entries.title: Range Sum Query - Mutable
entries.prerequisite: update(index,val) assigns a new value; it does not add val. Query endpoints are inclusive. Values may be negative.

entries.title: Sliding Window Maximum
entries.prerequisite: The official width satisfies 1 ≤ k ≤ n and returns maximum values only. The local example also returns the newest tied original index and handles a width larger than n.

entries.title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K
entries.prerequisite: The subarray must be nonempty, the target is positive, and negative input values are legal. Return -1 when absent; the local program returns None or a length/range witness.

entries.title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
entries.prerequisite: Strictly smaller excludes equal values. Process original positions right to left, query ranks below the current rank, then add this occurrence; do not sort away original position identity.

entries.title: Merge Sorted Array
entries.prerequisite: Use the sorted merge reasoning from Binary Search/Sorting and the frame-condition argument in section 4.

entries.title: Reverse Linked List
entries.prerequisite: Singly linked nodes and reversal from Linked Lists, Stacks & Queues; this is a proof-oriented revisit, not a new node tutorial.

entries.title: Same Tree
entries.prerequisite: Finite binary-tree structure and recursion from Trees and Complexity; sharing/cycles require a different contract.

entries.title: Pow(x, n)
entries.prerequisite: Reciprocals, the integer exponent proof here, and floating-point accuracy. The official statement excludes zero with a nonpositive exponent.

entries.title: Network Delay Time
entries.prerequisite: Nodes are labeled 1…n; edge delays may be zero. An unreachable node changes the final result to −1.

entries.title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
entries.prerequisite: Use the local dense Prim branch to avoid storing every pair; the official input has up to 1,000 distinct points.

entries.title: Course Schedule II
entries.prerequisite: An input pair [a,b] means b→a, and impossibility returns an empty array. A valid order need not be unique.

entries.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
entries.prerequisite: k stops means at most k+1 flight edges. Prices are positive; absence of a feasible route returns −1.

entries.title: Parallel Courses III
entries.prerequisite: The task guarantees a DAG and allows any number of concurrent courses. Vertex labels are 1-based but duration positions are 0-based.

entries.title: Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors at a Threshold Distance
entries.prerequisite: Edges are bidirectional with positive weights. Count other cities; ties favor the greatest city index. Review Floyd–Warshall or repeated Dijkstra first.

entries.title: Minimum Cost to Make at Least One Valid Path in a Grid
entries.prerequisite: Review Graphs’ grid neighbor bounds and the local 0/1-deque branch. The objective counts sign changes, not moves; a sign may point outside the grid.

entries.title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
Shortest Palindrome
entries.prerequisite: Longest proper borders, a unique sentinel and the proof that the retained prefix must be palindromic.

entries.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
entries.prerequisite: Positive values, at most 200 items and values at most 100; review once-only subset DP.

entries.title: House Robber
entries.prerequisite: Nonnegative rewards; only neighboring positions conflict. The local path-independent-set example permits empty input and negative weights as additional cases.

entries.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
entries.prerequisite: At most 16 positive items; k nonempty parts, each with equal sum. Review backtracking ownership or DP subset state before attempting.

entries.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
Possible Bipartition
entries.prerequisite: BFS or DFS two-coloring; up to 2,000 people and 10,000 distinct conflicts. Every conflict must connect different parts.

entries.title: Maximum Students Taking Exam
entries.prerequisite: Grid coordinates, bipartite matching/cover and the complement identity: vertices outside a cover form an independent set. The official grid is at most 8×8; conflicts are horizontal or diagonal to the preceding row, not directly vertical.

entries.title: Check If It Is a Straight Line
Max Points on a Line
entries.prerequisite: Canonical integer direction pairs using gcd and a sign convention; hash-map grouping. These are developed in this lesson’s optional section.

entries.title: Snapshot Array
entries.prerequisite: Binary search for an upper bound; section 5 explains its history invariant.

entries.title: Time Based Key-Value Store
entries.prerequisite: Dictionary lookup, sorted histories and predecessor search; string values need no interval aggregate.

entries.title: LRU Cache
entries.prerequisite: Hash maps and a doubly linked recency list; the earlier linked-list and hashing lessons supply these mechanisms.

entries.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
entries.prerequisite: Heap-based k-way merging from Heaps, Priority Queues & Tries.

entries.title: Sort List
entries.prerequisite: Linked-list splitting/merging and iterative versus recursive auxiliary-space accounting.

entries.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
entries.prerequisite: Sorted row streams and a min-heap; binary-search alternatives require a separately justified counting predicate.

For directed graphs, ordinary reachability is not symmetric. If A→B exists without B→A, B is reachable from A but A is not reachable from B. Running this undirected component-labeling routine on outgoing directed edges does not compute strongly connected components. A strongly connected component requires mutual reachability; a weak component ignores direction. State which question is intended before applying a component algorithm.
• Princeton: Directed Graphs — directed reachability, cycle detection, topological and strongly connected structure.

<Prose>Bitmasks can compactly encode a finite used-set, but that changes representation rather than proving the search correct. This lesson uses explicit sets first. Before adopting mask-based search or DP, learn membership bits, bitwise versus Boolean operations, width/sign/shift semantics and the state key's meaning. An unexplained XOR or shift trick should not replace the constraint invariant.</Prose>
['Remove a member', 'mask & ~(1 << i)', 'Clear that bit; unlike XOR, this also works when absent'],
['Toggle membership', 'mask ^ (1 << i)', 'XOR flips the bit; it is not unconditional removal'],

<RunnableExample example={dynamicProgrammingExamples.masks}><Prose>Python integers do not overflow at a fixed 32- or 64-bit width. Bitwise operations behave as if there were infinitely many sign bits, so ~5 is −6, not the four-bit complement 1010. Masking with full restricts a complement to the chosen finite universe. A negative shift count is an error; for nonnegative i, left shift multiplies by 2ⁱ and right shift uses floor division by 2ⁱ. The browser model uses only tiny masks that fit JavaScript's 32-bit bitwise range.</Prose></RunnableExample>
• Python · integer bitwise operations — exact shift, complement and sign semantics; distinguish these from bounded-width browser masks.

If a positive integer ends with a 1 followed by k zeros in binary, lowbit is 2ᵏ. In a sufficient two's-complement width, negating flips the bits and adds one: the trailing zeros stay zero, that lowest 1 stays one, and every higher bit becomes the opposite. Bitwise AND therefore retains only that 1. Thus i & -i isolates the low bit. For 6: 0110 AND 1010 = 0010, giving 2. Python defines these integer bitwise operations as though negative integers had indefinitely many leading sign bits, so the same identity holds for positive i without choosing a fixed width.
• Python · integer bitwise semantics — unlimited-precision integers, sign extension and bit_length; the low-bit derivation does not assume an arbitrary fixed Python integer width.
